name: Bakbuk
title: Temple Servant After the Exile
summary: Bakbuk was the ancestor of one of the families among the temple servants (netinim) who returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. His descendants are mentioned in the lists of those who returned with Zerubbabel to rebuild the temple and restore worship in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Listed Among the Temple Servants in Ezra's List
keyEvents.description: Bakbuk's descendants are mentioned among the temple servants (netinim) who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel.

keyEvents.title: Listed Among the Temple Servants in Nehemiah's List
keyEvents.description: In Nehemiah's parallel list of those who returned from exile, Bakbuk's descendants are again mentioned among the temple servants.

keyEvents.title: The Role of the Temple Servants in the Rebuilding
keyEvents.description: The temple servants, including Bakbuk's descendants, settled in Jerusalem and contributed to restoring temple service after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Registration of Returning Families
keyEvents.description: The family of Bakbuk was carefully registered as part of the official work to document who had the right to serve in the temple after returning from Babylon.
